scope: Finite adapter source review and synthetic CPU tests only.
checks: Deep-copied complete caller identity; explicit experimental p198 contract; exact store-root and store-binary/owner-binary binding; ready context/vocabulary/one-load checks.
One reentrant owner mutex spans policy lookup, RUN, postreply parking and disposition. No launch, signal, restart, HTTP or checkpoint serialization operation.

SAVE requires current reply identity and exact full visible IDs, fresh checkpoint ID, conservative free-space admission, manifest hash acknowledgement and validated locked snapshot with identical history.
Append intent captures manifest hash/input once, is revalidated against actual max_new before RUN and consumed on attempt; same-generation resume is refused by this API.
All normally completed no-SAVE policy paths release pending reply, including non-None same-ID reuse; final release may leave front draining for coordinator stop/exit checks.
Any exception poisons further intake; no automatic RELEASE/retry/close/signal after ambiguity; Parking retained reservations remain charged.
limitations: All13 tests use synthetic metadata and mocked front/store objects; no native integration qualification is inferred.
Trusted launch provenance must attest actual owner binary/startup checkpoint root; ready protocol does not attest those values.
Size-bound proof remains injected and caller-owned; accepted256MiB proof is restricted to the exact p198 real-model identity/context4096.

Constructor intentionally requires identical store-tool and admitted owner binary SHA. A GNU-host tool inspecting device-binary checkpoints proves only Store+Bridge, not actual device-owner adapter attachment.
Native restore must perform full state validation again before upload; metadata snapshots do not validate tensor contents.
